name: Fethiye
title: Holidays in Fethiye
intro: A harbour town on Turkey's turquoise coast, close to the famous Ölüdeniz lagoon, paragliding, rock tombs and boat trips to hidden coves. Here's what Fethiye is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The long beach at Ölüdeniz near Fethiye, curving below green mountains

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 2 hrs ahead of the UK (3 in winter)

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: No visa for up to 90 days

facts_note: Your passport needs at least 150 days left on it when you arrive. Check entry rules and the latest travel advice on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June, September and October are best, warm with a warm sea and fewer crowds. July and August are very hot, often 34°C or more. Winter is mild but many resorts close.

things.name: Ölüdeniz Blue Lagoon
things.blurb: A calm, shallow lagoon with a sandy spit, about 20 minutes away.

things.name: Paragliding from Babadağ
things.blurb: Tandem flights high above Ölüdeniz, one of the world's top spots.

things.name: 12 Islands boat trip
things.blurb: A day of swimming in coves around Fethiye bay.

things.name: Lycian rock tombs
things.blurb: Temple-fronted tombs cut into the cliff above town.

things.name: Kayaköy

things.name: Saklıkent Gorge

faqs.question: Is Fethiye worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's a working town with a great market, and it's close to Ölüdeniz, boat trips and the Lycian Way.

faqs.question: How do you get to Fethiye?
faqs.answer: Fly into Dalaman, which has many direct flights from the UK, then drive about 45 minutes.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Fethiye?
faqs.answer: May, June, September and October, around 22 to 31°C.

faqs.question: Should you stay in Fethiye or Ölüdeniz?
faqs.answer: Ölüdeniz is right on the beach but touristy. Fethiye has more of a real town, with a market and harbour.

faqs.question: Is Fethiye good for families?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Ölüdeniz lagoon is calm and shallow, and boat trips are a hit with children.
